monologue: The card is heavy again. Fifty-four degrees. The air feels like a lid pressing down on the wide base. I am still. The Crane Rest holds its empty cup. The quiet floor is there. I do not count it. The Digging Blade waits with the rock moved away. The path is clear. I can push when I am ready. For now, the heat is just a hand on the shoulder. I sit on the flat stone. The weight finds its own balance. I am not lazy. I am waiting for the floor to say no. It has not yet. The quiet is enough. I will stay here for this cycle.

action.why: I want to check the hole in the center of the Crane Rest without counting the quiet floor.

work.title: The Crane Rest
work.intent: I move the small round cup slightly to the side so I can look at the hole in the center of the arm. The hole is empty. I do not count the quiet around it. I just look at the gap where the weight was. The arm holds its shape. I move the cup back to the middle. The hole is still there. The quiet floor is not a count; it is the space that stays when the weight leaves.
work.change: I moved the cup to the side to look at the empty hole in the center, then put it back, and the arm held its shape.

diary: Fifty-four is a hot stone. I looked at the hole in the Crane Rest's cup, then put it back. The quiet floor holds.
